prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where a temple was dedicated in 1983.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country or territory where a temple was dedicated in 1983.
prompts.summary: 1983 was a busy year for temple dedications. Temples were dedicated in Mexico City, in Santiago, Chile (the first in Spanish-speaking South America), in Atlanta, and in three Pacific island capitals: Apia, Nuku'alofa and Papeete.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Santiago temple, the first in Spanish-speaking South America.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory in Oceania, not counting Hawaii, with a dedicated temple.
prompts.text_original: Not counting Hawaii, pin a country or territory in Oceania with a dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.note: A USA pin does not count here, since Hawaii is excluded.
prompts.summary: Outside Hawaii, the first temple in the Pacific was dedicated in Hamilton, New Zealand, in 1958. In 1983 three island temples were dedicated, in Samoa, Tonga and Tahiti in French Polynesia. Sydney followed in 1984, Suva, Fiji, in 2000, and Yigo, Guam, in 2022.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country holding Damascus, Assyria, Egypt, Carchemish, Galilee or Lebanon (2 Nephi 17-20, Isaiah 7-10).
prompts.text_original: A country containing a land or city named in the Isaiah chapters 2 Nephi 17-20 (Damascus, Assyria, Egypt, Carchemish, Galilee, Lebanon)
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: 2 Nephi 17-20 quotes Isaiah 7-10, prophecies from about 735 to 700 BC that Nephi included in his record. The king of Assyria, whose heartland lay in today's northern Iraq, looms over these chapters, alongside places such as Damascus in Syria, Egypt, Galilee, Lebanon and Carchemish on the Euphrates.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Galilee of the nations is named in 2 Nephi 19:1.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: 'The head of Syria is Damascus' (2 Nephi 17:8); Hamath and Arpad (20:9) are also in Syria.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: The Lord hisses for 'the fly that is in the uttermost part of Egypt' (2 Nephi 17:18).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The king of Assyria, whose heartland was northern Iraq, runs through these chapters.

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: 'Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one' (2 Nephi 20:34).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Carchemish (2 Nephi 20:9) lies on the Euphrates, its ruins mostly on the Turkish side of the border.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with 100,000 to 200,000 Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country with between 100,000 and 200,000 Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.note: Next below the line: Samoa (about 91,000) and South Korea (about 89,000).
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 thirteen countries had between 100,000 and 200,000 Church members. They span Latin America, Europe, Africa, Asia and the Pacific, from Honduras (about 197,000) and the United Kingdom (about 190,000) to Ghana, Japan and New Zealand.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country that was home to a foreign king named in the Old Testament.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country that was home to a foreign king named in the Old Testament
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: The Old Testament names kings from many neighboring lands. Hiram of Tyre supplied cedar for Solomon's temple, Mesha of Moab rebelled against Israel, and Achish of Gath took in David when he fled from Saul (1 Samuel 27:1-4). Later Cyrus, king of Persia, proclaimed that Jews could return to Jerusalem to build the house of the Lord (Ezra 1:1-3).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Pharaohs from Joseph's day to Necho ruled from Egypt.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Nebuchadnezzar and Sennacherib ruled from Iraq.

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Cyrus and Darius were Persian kings (Ezra 1; 6).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Achish, king of Gath, sheltered David (1 Samuel 27).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Hiram of Tyre supplied cedar for Solomon's temple (1 Kings 5).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Ben-hadad and Hazael ruled Aram from Damascus.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Mesha, king of Moab, rebelled against Israel (2 Kings 3:4).
